findings.title: Multipart uploads have no server-side input limit before ImageMagick processing
findings.body: The new 10 MB limit is only enforced by the browser and for URL downloads; a client can POST a multipart file directly with any size. Any oversized image is passed through up to five ImageMagick conversions before `Upload.create_for` gets a chance to enforce the configured stored-file limit. An upload-capable user can therefore submit very large or decompression-bomb images and consume substantial worker CPU, memory, disk, and temporary-file space. Enforce a raw byte and image-pixel limit on the server before invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize`.

findings.title: The new downsize definition replaces, rather than overloads, the existing API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count. This definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts = {})` definition, so existing callers using the prior width/height API now either raise `ArgumentError` for five arguments or treat `max_height` as `opts` for four arguments and fail when `optimize` indexes it as a hash. Preserve both call forms in a single method or use a differently named helper.

findings.title: Oversized animated GIF uploads lose their animation despite the setting
findings.body: For normal multipart uploads, `tempfile.path` is Rack's generated temporary filename rather than the original `.gif` filename. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated GIF path only when `from` ends in `.GIF`; this call therefore takes the regular ImageMagick path, whose input is `#{from}[0]` and contains only the first frame. Consequently, an oversized animated GIF is converted to a static image even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled. Preserve/pass the original format when selecting the conversion path and write through a suitably typed temporary file.

findings.title: The retry limit does not ensure the image meets the configured size limit
findings.body: The loop stops after five 80%-dimension resizes without checking that the resulting byte size is below `max_image_size_kb`. File size is not reduced by a fixed ratio when dimensions are reduced, especially for PNGs and already-compressed images, and valid installations can configure a limit low enough that five passes are insufficient. The subsequent upload will then be rejected by the existing size validation (or stored over the intended limit), so users still cannot upload the large image the feature is meant to handle. Continue until the byte target is met or no further useful reduction is possible, and return a clear failure when it cannot be met.

findings.title: Client-side attachment limits no longer honor site configuration
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` is used for both `image` and `attachment`, but this change replaces the type-specific `max_<type>_size_kb` setting with a fixed 10 MB limit for both. Non-image attachments are not downsized by the controller, so sites with a smaller attachment limit now let users upload files that the server rejects, while sites allowing attachments over 10 MB are incorrectly blocked in the browser. Keep the larger raw-file allowance limited to images being downsized and continue using `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments.
